claim: Replacing the constant start (R=2/3) with a discretized Gaussian exp(-0.5((i-c)/sigma)^2) on N=2001 and optimizing sigma raises R to 0.7210, consistent with the analytic Gaussian value 1/sqrt(2)≈0.7071 (slightly above it due to discretization).

Random-restart hill climbing with block perturbations and progressive upsampling to fine resolution (N=3200) reaches R=0.8116, the best of generation 1, far above the Gaussian baseline 0.7210; the resulting f*f is much flatter-topped (16% of knots within 0.1% of max vs 1.1% for the Gaussian) with its peak shifted off-center to 0.29 of support.

Multiscale random multiplicative coordinate ascent from the constant start reaches R=0.7955 at N=400, second-best in generation 1, again producing a broad f*f top (2.75%/9.86%/28.71% of knots within 0.1%/1%/5% of max) with peak at 0.416 of support.

Parametric family search over generalized Gaussians exp(-|x|^p) and compact bumps (1-x^2)_+^a with golden-section refinement reaches only R=0.7238, barely above the pure Gaussian 0.7210; smooth symmetric parametric families are near-optimal within their class but cannot match the non-parametric hill-climbed shapes (0.81).

Naive single-coordinate multiplicative hill climbing from a random exponential start (N=1000, sigma=0.2, restarts every 5000 non-improving steps) stalls at R=0.6567, below even the constant 2/3; single-coordinate moves on a high-dimensional shape are too weak to escape the random start.

Higher R correlates with a flatter, broader f*f top and an off-center peak: the best constructions (p0003 R=0.812, p0004 R=0.796) have 16% and 2.75% of knots within 0.1% of max with peaks at 0.29 and 0.42 of support, versus 1.1% and peak at 0.50 for the Gaussian (p0005 R=0.721); flattening the autoconvolution maximum relative to its L2 mass is the operative lever.

Coarse global differential-evolution search over all N=32 heights from scratch, followed by coordinate/block descent and progressive 2x upsampling to N=2048, reaches R=0.852088 — the best result of any generation, beating the previous best 0.8116 by +0.0405 — with a distinct basin: f*f peak at 0.805 of support (vs 0.290 for p0003, 0.520 for p0008) and a flatter top (15.2%/35.7%/42.0% of knots with

The 0.8116 barrier is a basin artifact, not a global bound: smooth-start local methods (gradient and coordinate) all converge to the same few basins (peaks at 0.29 and 0.52), while a derivative-free global search at N=32 opens a genuinely different basin (peak 0.805) that refines to 0.8521. This confirms F12's suspicion that p0003 was only the best smooth-start basin.

Annealed smoothed-max (p-norm) gradient ascent at N=3200 (p=4..64) does not move p0011 off 0.811595: +0.000000, identical score and identical plateau fraction (16.03% within 0.1%). Smoothing the max kink gives a non-zero gradient but no usable descent direction at this optimum, so the kink is not what blocks improvement.

Exact-gradient Adam ascent with multiscale upsampling applied to p0008 (N=6400) leaves the score unchanged at 0.803448 (+0.000000), confirming again that gradient methods are a no-op on these optima while coordinate descent still gains (p0019 +0.000588 on the same start).

Adaptive block coordinate descent (blocks of width 1..N/20, step-size feedback, perturb-restarts, resampling to N=12800/25600/51200) on p0008's distinct basin (peak 0.52) raises R from 0.803448 to 0.804037 (+0.000588) but stalls well below 0.8116; the peak stays at 0.520 and the plateau fraction grows only slightly (4.02% -> 4.63% within 0.1%). The 0.52-peak basin appears to top out near 0.804.

Upsampling p0010's construction to N=8001 and running finer block refinement with keep() after every climb raises R from 0.785486 to 0.786976 (+0.001490), with the f*f peak moving to 0.484 and a much sharper top (0.41% within 0.1%). Confirms that resolution resampling plus coordinate climbing still yields small gains on the Gaussian-derived basin, but far below the global-search basin.

Mass-preserving upsampling of p0018's N=2048 construction to N=4096/8192/16384 with adaptive random-block descent and per-coordinate polish does not raise R: 0.852088 -> 0.852089 (+0.000001) in 28.3 s CPU. Analytic-gradient Adam ascent on log R with upsampling through N=8192, plus coordinate polish and perturb/restart loops, leaves p0018's construction unchanged at R=0.852088 (+0.000000), peak 0.805, plateau 15.23% within 0.1%. Gradient methods are again a no-op on an already-optimized optimum, this time in the new global-DE basin, confirming the pattern is not specific to the 0.29/0.52-peak basins.

Smoothed-max (p-norm) gradient annealing at low N plus cumulative-mass upsampling, exact-R polish and perturbed restarts leaves p0017's construction at R=0.811595 (+0.000000), peak 0.290, plateau 16.03% within 0.1%. Replacing the exact-max kink with a smoothed max still yields no movement, so the vanishing gradient at these optima is not solely the max-kink effect.

Upsampling p0017's construction to N=200000 immediately and polishing with the exact gradient at full resolution fails on the step cap: the run reached N=204800 and was rejected (too many steps, limit 200000), with the last printed score still 0.811595. High-resolution upsampling of an existing optimum costs steps without moving R, so it must be budgeted against the step limit, not just CPU.

Applying the same N=64 coarse-DE + upsample-to-6400 recipe to p0024's distinct 0.468-peak basin (R=0.819750) yields only +0.000052 (to 0.819802), far short of the predicted 0.83-0.85. The 0.468-peak basin is also saturated under this recipe; the +0.008 that p0024 got came from the initial coarse-DE discovery, not from repeated refinement.

A structured sum-of-K=6-free-rectangular-blocks family (centers, widths, heights; 18 params; DE then block/coordinate descent, rasterized to N=2048) did not finish within budget: the run stopped at the 47 s CPU limit with nothing kept because keep_best was wired to a stale variable. No score was produced, so the block family remains untested as a construction.

Replacing coordinate descent with FFT-based analytic-gradient Adam ascent on log R (plus block moves and perturb/restart) on p0014's N=32001 construction crashed with an IndexError: a boolean mask of length 16001 was applied to an array of length 32001. The gradient machinery itself was never evaluated; the failure is a shape bug in the block-perturbation mask, not evidence about gradient methods.

Analytic-gradient ascent of R (FFT-based) plus block descent and localized perturbations, applied to p0023's N=4096 construction, leaves the score unchanged at 0.852089 (+0.000000), with plateau fraction 15.27% within 0.1% and peak at 0.485. This is a fourth independent confirmation that gradient methods are a no-op on these optima.

Mass-preserving upsampling of p0023 from N=4096 through 8192 to 16384 with block-move descent and per-coordinate fine polish leaves R unchanged at 0.852089 (+0.000000), plateau 15.26% within 0.1%. This reproduces F19's saturation result on the same basin via a different code path, strengthening the claim that the 0.852 basin is locally saturated at N<=16384.

A free-knot piecewise-constant construction (K=8 segments, 7 free breakpoints + 8 free heights, 15 params, rasterized to N=2048) optimized by differential evolution then block/coordinate descent reaches R=0.832956 from scratch — a distinct basin (peak at 0.500, 1.17% plateau within 0.1%) that beats the Gaussian baseline 0.7210 and the parametric-family ceiling 0.7238, but falls short of the unifor

Simulated-annealing basin hopping with structured block/Fourier perturbations plus block descent and coordinate polish raises the saturated 0.8198 basin (p0030) by +0.000225 to 0.820028 at N=6400, with the f*f peak moving to 0.547 and plateau 8.14% within 0.1%. Enlarging the N=64 coarse DE (popsize 40, one third uniform-random init, one third heavily perturbed seed, 7 s cap, upsample through N=1024) does not find a better coarse basin than p0029's popsize-15 seeded DE: R stays at 0.852108 (+0.000000), plateau 15.81% within 0.1%, peak at 0.716. Broader random-diverse coarse search does not escape the 0.852 basin.

Normalized-momentum analytic-gradient ascent on log R with mass-preserving upsampling to N=8192 and block coordinate polish leaves the 0.852 basin unchanged at 0.852088 (+0.000000), plateau 15.25% within 0.1%, peak at 0.805 — another confirmation that gradient methods are a no-op on these optima.

FFT-based analytic-gradient Adam ascent on R plus upsample+Adam+polish to N=8192 leaves p0023's construction at 0.852089 (+0.000000), plateau 15.26% within 0.1%, peak at 0.715. Reproduces F29/F30's saturation of the 0.852 basin under gradient refinement.

Corrected mass-resampling plus smoothed-max annealing at N=1200 with more p values and upsampling to N=40000 with longer exact-R polish and more perturbed restarts leaves the 0.29-peak basin at 0.811595 (-0.000000), plateau 16.03% within 0.1%, peak at 0.290. The 0.29-peak basin remains saturated under smoothed-max annealing regardless of resolution and budget.

Simulated-annealing basin hopping with structured perturbations (block-multiply, low-frequency Fourier, bump, global) applied to the saturated 0.852 basin at N=2048 raises R from 0.852108 to 0.852591 (+0.000483), the first escape from that basin after greedy descent, coarse DE, and mass-upsampling all failed; the f*f peak moves to 0.507 and the 0.1% plateau fraction rises to 16.82%.

Warm-starting a richer K=16 free-knot piecewise-constant DE from p0037's quantile-segmented shape, then SA basin hopping and block descent at N=4096, raises R from 0.832956 to 0.839015 (+0.006058); the result has a much sharper top (1.78%/12.66% within 0.1%/1%) and peak at 0.381, showing the free-knot family is not saturated at K=8.

A log-piecewise-linear (exponential-spline) parametrization — K=10 knots, 8 free interior positions, u_i in [-3,3], h=exp(u), 18 params — optimized by DE then block/SA polish reaches R=0.831320 from scratch at N=1024, a distinct asymmetric basin (peak at 0.594, 4.69% plateau within 0.1%, max/mean height 3.99), competitive with the free-knot line without any warm start.

Analytic-gradient Adam ascent on log R with mass-preserving upsampling to N=2048 and alternating Adam/block restarts leaves the 0.852 basin unchanged at 0.852108 (+0.000000), plateau 15.84% within 0.1%, peak at 0.484 — another confirmation that gradient methods are a no-op on this optimum.

Analytic-gradient L-BFGS-B polishing with progressive upsampling to N=8192 and perturbation restarts leaves the 0.852 basin at 0.852109 (+0.000001), plateau 15.86% within 0.1%, peak at 0.806 — the second-order gradient method is as inert as Adam on this optimum.

FFT-based block descent plus mass-preserving upscaling across N levels and per-coordinate polish on p0004's 0.312-peak construction yields only +0.000016 (0.795501 -> 0.795517), plateau 2.75% within 0.1% — the 0.795 basin is saturated against this refiner as well.
